description: We are a focused team of developers and tech enthusiasts with backgrounds in Python backend architecture (FastAPI, SQLite), data analytics, and interactive web applications. Our goal is to build a reliable, intelligent health-monitoring system designed to track physiological metrics and support autonomous medical decision-making during long-duration space missions.
summary:
Inner Climate is an offline web tool that lets astronauts on long missions check their own physical and mental health and get clear next steps. It shows the body and mind as “weather” outside the base window, so a drop in sleep, mood or vitals looks like a storm coming in, without needing medical training to read the charts.

The project has two parts. The astronaut monitor includes a 3D anatomy atlas with problem zones highlighted, trends and forecasts by sol, a psychological diary, and a help ladder that goes from self-care to the onboard medic to a doctor, with an auto-generated summary for the doctor. There are also stress-relief Mission Games and Family Connection: animated family portraits, voice messages and a view of Earth from the cabin. The crew site “Orbita” tracks required check-ups, fitness-for-duty status and the team’s psychological climate.

This matters because on Mars, communication delays of up to 20+ minutes mean crews can’t wait for Earth. Inner Climate runs fully offline from a single file. It catches problems early, keeps isolated crews emotionally connected to home, and supports their autonomy, the core of the challenge.
details:
website - https://whytee16.github.io/Astro-Health-Monitoring/

What it does and how it works
Inner Climate is an offline health-monitoring platform for astronauts on long-duration missions. It has two parts. The astronaut monitor (index.html) is a personal tool for daily self-assessment. The crew site “Orbita” (crew.html) is a shared overview for the whole team. The astronaut’s condition is shown as “weather” outside the base window: clear skies when everything is fine, a storm when sleep, mood or vital signs are declining. Anyone can read their status at a glance, without medical training.

Key modules: an interactive 3D anatomy atlas (male/female models with peelable layers and glowing problem zones); trends and forecasts for each mission sol with a full mission calendar; a 5-question psychological diary with automatic insights; a help ladder (self-care → onboard medic → doctor) that generates a summary for the doctor; Mission Games for stress relief (breathing, memory, a space garden); Family Connection (animated family photos, voice and video messages, a view of Earth from the cabin); and a 3D avatar that walks the base toward daily goals. The crew site tracks required check-ups, fitness-for-duty status and the team’s psychological climate.

Benefits and intended impact
On Mars, a signal delay of up to 20+ minutes each way means crews can’t rely on real-time help from Earth. Inner Climate catches problems early, gives clear next steps, and supports crew autonomy. Just as important, it fights isolation and keeps astronauts emotionally connected to home and to each other. The same approach could help people in other isolated settings: polar stations, submarines and remote workers.

Tools and technologies
HTML5, CSS3 and vanilla JavaScript; Three.js for the 3D planets, anatomy and base; WebXR and a stereo mode for VR headsets; localStorage and IndexedDB for private on-device storage; Python for the build script and automated tests. Planet surfaces use NASA maps (Blue Marble, LRO, Viking/MOLA, Cassini), with credits listed in the project. Everything is bundled into files that open with a double click, with no server, internet or installation needed.

Creativity
We turned dry medical data into a visual metaphor: weather. We added gamification (experience, credits, a shop for customizing your character and personal cabin) so that daily check-ins feel motivating instead of tiring. Family portraits that “breathe” and speak in a loved one’s voice make home feel close.

Factors we considered
Working with no connection to Earth; privacy (all data stays on the device); ease of use under stress and fatigue; psychological safety (no penalties for skipped days); international crews (full English and Russian, plus key interface text in Kazakh, Chinese, Japanese, French, German and Spanish). We also made clear that this is an educational prototype, not a medical device.
